title: Feasibility of Remote Blood Pressure Monitoring to Improve Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy
official: SH RBPM: Feasibility of Remote Blood Pressure Monitoring to Improve Management of Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy
summary: This study represents an innovative approach to hypertensive disorders of pregnancy surveillance by using remote blood pressure monitoring to address the unique challenges of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy management in a predominantly rural state. Transitioning from episodic in-clinic monitoring to continuous, patient-centered monitoring changes how high-risk patients and healthcare providers detect hypertensive episodes and advances the field by establishing clinical effectiveness and feasibility of remote blood pressure monitoring (RBPM), to provide evidence for scaling interventions that improve maternal health.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Women aged 18 years or older
2. Either currently pregnant or within 10 days postpartum
3. Singleton pregnancy
4. Diagnosed with a hypertensive disorder during the current or the most recent pregnancy
5. Able and willing to provide informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Men will not be included in the study
2. Women younger than 18 years of age
3. Women with a multiple gestation pregnancy
4. Those without a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy
